entity_title: EU nationals get a registration card, not a residence permit
fact_text: An EU/EEA/Swiss national exercising free movement in Latvia is issued a Registration Card of the Union Citizen confirming a right they already hold; it is not a residence permit that grants the right, and the service is free of charge. Non-EU family members instead receive a residence permit.
evidence_quote: Registration Card of the Union Citizen is issued if a citizen of the Union or his/her family member, who is a citizen of the Union, resides in the Republic of Latvia for a definite period.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR teams used to third-country permits assume EU staff also need a 'permit'; in Latvia they get a declaratory Registration Card (free), and only non-EU family members get an actual permit.

entity_title: Registration certificate required for stays over 90 days
fact_text: An EU citizen who plans to stay in Latvia longer than 90 days must request the certificate of registration of the citizen of the European Union from the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP). A short stay under 90 days needs nothing.
evidence_quote: If a citizen of another state of the European Union plans to permanently stay in Latvia for longer than 90 days, he or she shall request a certificate of registration of the citizen of the European Union.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The 90-day line is the trigger for the whole registration/personal-code/tax/health cascade; below it nothing is required, above it registration is mandatory.

entity_title: PMLP decides the residence document within 30 days
fact_text: Once documents are submitted, PMLP takes its decision on issuing the residence document within 30 days. Because the personal code, address declaration, tax status and state healthcare all cascade from this step, it should be started on arrival, not deferred.
evidence_quote: A decision on the issuance of a permanent residence certificate shall be taken within 30 days.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR often treats EU registration as a same-day formality; the statutory decision window is up to 30 days, and downstream steps (payroll, health cover) cannot complete until the personal code is issued.

entity_title: Personal code (personas kods) comes with the registration certificate
fact_text: An EU citizen obtains the Latvian personal identity number (personas kods) by requesting the EU registration certificate at PMLP; there is no separate application. The personas kods is the master key for payroll, tax (VID), social insurance (VSAA), state healthcare and banking. A visa never confers a personal code.
evidence_quote: It should be taken into account that visa does not give the right to the personal identity number.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The personas kods is not requested on its own; for EU nationals it is issued through the registration certificate, and everything else (bank account, e-services, payroll, health) is gated on having it.

entity_title: Address must be declared within one month (deklareta dzivesvieta)
fact_text: After settling in, a person has a legal duty to declare their place of residence within one month of habitually living there. EU citizens can only declare once they hold a registration or permanent residence certificate. Declaring online via Latvija.lv is free; declaring in person costs EUR 4.27.
evidence_quote: in case of change of the place of residence the person shall have a duty within one month, since the person habitually lives at the new place of residence, to declare it in the institution of declaration of the place of residence.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The declared address is not just admin: it is one of the two statutory triggers of Latvian tax residency (see LV:employment:tax_residency), so a routine address declaration silently flips tax status.

entity_title: Employer must register a new hire with VID BEFORE they start work
fact_text: The employer must report a new employee to the State Revenue Service (VID) before the person starts work: at least one hour before via the Electronic Declaration System, or one day before if filed on paper. Missing this is an employer-side breach, not the employee's problem.
evidence_quote: for persons who start working: no later than within one day before the person starts his/her work, if information is submitted in paper form, or no later than within one hour before the person starts his/her work, if information is submitted electronically in the Electronic Declaration System

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A common HR trap: registration is due BEFORE the first working hour, not within days after start; a foreign employer onboarding in Latvia can be non-compliant on day one.

entity_title: Social contributions (VSAOI) are due from the first day of employment
fact_text: Mandatory state social insurance contributions (VSAOI) are payable from the day a person acquires employee status, with no waiting period. The combined rate for full coverage is 34.09% (employer 23.59%, employee 10.50%).
evidence_quote: An employee is socially insured against all social risks, and mandatory contributions (VSAOI) must be made from the day the person acquires employee status.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: There is no grace period: coverage and the 34.09% liability attach from the very first day of employee status, which matters for mid-month starts and short assignments.

entity_title: Minimum social contributions apply even to low or part-time pay
fact_text: Latvia enforces a minimum mandatory contribution base (EUR 2 340 per quarter / EUR 780 per month in 2026). If an employee's declared income falls below it, the employer must make additional top-up contributions up to the minimum object, so part-time or low-paid staff still generate a contribution floor.
evidence_quote: The employer and the self-employed person must make additional payments up to the minimum contribution object.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Employers assume contributions track actual pay; below the minimum base the employer owes a top-up, an unexpected cost for part-time, hourly or partial-month hires.

entity_title: State healthcare access is tied to actually-paid contributions
fact_text: State health insurance is funded by 1% of the 34.09% VSAOI rate, and a person is treated as covered only if contributions have actually been made. Employment alone does not guarantee cover if the employer fails to pay; coverage follows the paid contribution, not the contract.
evidence_quote: Out of the total 34.09% rate, 1% is allocated to healthcare service funding. All employees and self-employed persons who have actually made contributions to health insurance are considered covered by the state health insurance system.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Latvia's mandatory-health-insurance model links state healthcare to the social insurance system; the word 'actually' matters - unpaid contributions can leave a nominally-employed person without state cover.

entity_title: State-funded healthcare requires a job or self-employment, not just residence
fact_text: State-funded healthcare is provided to EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who have entered into labour relationships or reside as self-employed persons in Latvia (and their family members). Merely residing in Latvia as an EU citizen without working does not by itself open state healthcare.
evidence_quote: State-funded health care services are provided in Latvia to: citizens of Latvia; non-citizens of Latvia; citizens of the EU Member States, Island, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, who have entered into labour relationships or reside as self-employed persons in Latvia

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A genuine non-obvious gap: an EU relocatee who is registered and resident but not yet working (e.g. accompanying spouse, gap before starting) is not automatically in the state health system - cover follows employment/self-employment.

entity_title: You can be health-insured in only one country (S1 form)
fact_text: A person can be health-insured in only one EU/EEA state at a time. If you live in Latvia but remain insured (employed, pensioner) in another EU/EEA state, the UK or Switzerland, you need an S1 form registered with the National Health Service to get Latvian state healthcare. S1 registration is refused if the person is insured or employed in Latvia.
evidence_quote: Registration of the S1 form will be refused if the person is insured (employed or receiving a pension) in Latvia.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Cross-border cases (working remotely for a home-country employer, or a posted worker) hinge on which state you are insured in; you cannot double up, and the S1/A1 coordination decides where health cover sits.

entity_title: State-funded care still carries patient co-payments
fact_text: Even for state-funded services the patient pays a patient contribution (a small part of the total cost), with the state covering the larger part at unified approved rates. Latvian public healthcare is subsidised, not fully free at the point of use.
evidence_quote: If the state-funded services are obtained, then patients pay patient contributions (which is a small part from the total costs of services), and the biggest part of the service costs are covered by the state in accordance with the unified service rates approved in the state.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Relocatees expecting fully free public healthcare are surprised by patient co-payments; the state covers most but not all of each service.
